evidence: The survivor comments that "u,w values cancel out in equality test" and precomputes "forbidden color pairs"; its solver therefore treats the task as graph coloring with colors 1, 2, and 3.
affordance_in_statement: For linked nodes, the statement defines V_u = x^2 · (w · x + u · y) + y^2 · (x^2 + y) and V_w = y^2 · (u · y + w · x) + x^2 · (y^2 + x), with x and y restricted to {1, 2, 3}.
removal_suggestion: Alter one diagnostic expression by adding an endpoint- and speed-dependent perturbation that preserves the supplied examples but makes some unequal speed pairs resonant as well. This prevents equality from simplifying to exactly x = y and makes the constraint genuinely edge-dependent.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Algebraically simplifies the resonance test to forbidding equal speeds, then solves the resulting 3-colorability instance.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The paired formulas for V_u and V_w, together with x,y in {1,2,3} and positive node labels, make the endpoint-dependent terms cancel in the equality test.

common_affordance: The resonance equations collapse to the constraint x != y, turning the problem into ordinary 3-coloring.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its search/backtracking approach exceeded the time limit on the worst-case n = 40 instances.
It explicitly enumerates all 3^n assignments using product([1, 2, 3], repeat=n), which times out for n = 40.

recommended_edit: Modify one of the V_u/V_w formulas with a non-canceling endpoint-dependent term, selected so the displayed examples retain their stated validity, so that the forbidden speed pairs depend on the actual edge endpoints rather than being exactly the equal-speed pairs.
